newsitem.title: UK: YEAREND-Spain share markets to rise, eyes on EMU.
newsitem.headline: YEAREND-Spain share markets to rise, eyes on EMU.

text.p: Shares in Madrid's two main stock indices will better recent all-time highs by some 15 percent in 1997 but the long-term outlook depends on whether Spain joins the first phase of European monetary union, a Reuters survey of the outlook for world stock markets showed on Wednesday.

The average prediction from eight Spanish analysts for the broad-based General Index of 106 stocks was for a rise to around 475 points by the end of the year. The same panel foresaw the Ibex-35 index of leading stocks touching 5,490.
The record for the General Index is 411.42 and for the Ibex-35 4,758.22, both scored on December 3. The indices stood at around 407 and 4,707 at midsession on Wednesday.
Following is a selection of quotes from analysts who contributed forecasts for Spain:
PHILIPPE SARDET, HEAD OF EQUITY SALES AT CREDIT LYONNAIS SECURITIES ESPANA
"These forecasts presuppose Spain's entry in the first phase of monetary union. If not, the General Index will end 1997 at 430 and 1998 at 450."
BANESTO ANALYST WHO DECLINED TO BE NAMED
"There will be possible volatility in 1997 depending on whether Spain makes it into the first group of EMU or not. Fuel for stocks should come from further rate cuts."
